title: Start Weight Training
meta_desc: Discover how to start weight training in NZ with our beginner's plan, including free weights, machines, compound movements, and progressive overload. Find the best NZ gyms for weight training and get fit with our expert advice.
intro: Weight training is an excellent way to improve overall fitness and health. As a beginner, it's essential to start with the right equipment and techniques. NZ gyms offer a range of options, from free weights to machines, to help you achieve your fitness goals.

sections.heading: Free Weights vs Machines
sections.body: When it comes to weight training, you have two primary options: free weights and machines. Free weights, such as dumbbells and barbells, provide a more comprehensive workout and help improve balance and coordination. Machines, on the other hand, target specific muscle groups and can be easier to use for beginners. City Fitness and Les Mills gyms in NZ have well-equipped free weights areas, while Jetts and Anytime Fitness have a range of machines to choose from.
list: Free weights: improve balance and coordination
Machines: target specific muscle groups, easier to use for beginners

sections.heading: Compound Movements
sections.body: Compound movements are exercises that work multiple muscle groups at once, such as squats, deadlifts, and bench press. These movements are essential for building overall strength and muscle mass. As a beginner, it's crucial to master these movements to progress in your weight training journey. Many NZ gyms, including City Fitness and Les Mills, offer group fitness classes that focus on compound movements.
list: Squats: work legs, glutes, and core
Deadlifts: work back, legs, and core
Bench press: work chest, shoulders, and triceps

sections.heading: Progressive Overload
sections.body: Progressive overload is the gradual increase of weight or resistance to challenge your muscles and promote growth. This can be achieved by increasing the weight, reps, or sets over time. It's essential to track your progress and adjust your workout routine accordingly. Anytime Fitness and Jetts gyms in NZ have a range of equipment to help you progress in your weight training journey.
list: Increase weight: challenge muscles and promote growth
Increase sets: improve overall strength and muscle mass

sections.heading: Best NZ Gyms for Weight Training
sections.body: When it comes to choosing the best NZ gym for weight training, consider the equipment, group fitness classes, and personal training options. City Fitness and Les Mills gyms have well-equipped free weights areas and offer a range of group fitness classes. Jetts and Anytime Fitness have a range of machines and equipment to suit all fitness levels.
list: City Fitness: well-equipped free weights area, group fitness classes
Les Mills: well-equipped free weights area, group fitness classes
Jetts: range of machines and equipment, 24/7 access
Anytime Fitness: range of machines and equipment, 24/7 access

sections.heading: Getting Started with Exercise NZ's Subsidised Gym Scheme
sections.body: Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme offers 40-70% off gym memberships for eligible individuals. This scheme can help you get started with weight training and improve your overall fitness and health. Check if you're eligible and find a participating gym near you.

sections.heading: Conclusion and Next Steps
sections.body: Starting weight training can seem daunting, but with the right equipment, techniques, and mindset, you can achieve your fitness goals. Remember to start with compound movements, progress gradually, and choose a gym that suits your needs. Take the first step towards a healthier and fitter you.
